subject: Re: Implementation wiring for no-train commitment and subprocessor KMS requests
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@mediflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@mediflow.com>; Procurement <procurement@mediflow.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA asks: no-train + KMS residency + subprocessor list

Ben / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal scoped a few items we need to resolve before we can get to signature:

- A binding "no-training / no-model-improvement" commitment for tenant inputs (we need precise language and an ops path to validate).
- KMS residency/onshore key control for any tokens/keys used in customer-specific encryption (Can you confirm which clouds and regions support onshore KMS for our US-only deployment?).
- Full subprocessor inventory (current + planned) with a short description of what data each subprocessor sees.

If you can provide a short ops checklist we can hand to our security team (what evidence you'll produce and who owns each step), that will speed review. Procurement would also appreciate an estimation of any SLA exceptions needed to meet these controls.

Can we target a timeline of next-week signoff if we can tick these boxes?

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Security & Privacy, Mediflow Health
alex.johnson@mediflow.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@mediflow.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks: no-train + KMS residency + subprocessor list

Alex —

Thanks — we can absolutely get you what you need. High level response and proposed next steps:

1) No-train wording: we can commit to a contractual no-training clause that is scoped to "customer-provided inputs and outputs" (we'll propose authoritative contract language in the DPA addendum). Operationally we'll:
   - Disable model-update pipelines for tenant-labeled capture for your account by default.
   - Provide an audit snapshot (hash + timestamped manifest) showing training-pipeline isolation for a given date range.

2) KMS residency: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS in US regions (we support AWS KMS with customer-owned keys and Azure KeyVault in US East/West zones). We'll produce a short table of supported combos and an ops note describing how keys are mounted and rotated.

3) Subprocessors: attached is an export of the current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory.csv). We'll also include a short "who sees what" column. For planned subprocessors we can provide a 30-day notice and a gating workflow.

Attachments I'll push to the Drive folder listed below and upload a PDF checklist (no-train-evidence-checklist.pdf) that maps each contractual ask to an operational artifact (logs, manifests, snapshots).

Next steps suggested:
- Kimberly / David to confirm minimal ops artifacts (what we'll hand to Mediflow security).
- Legal teams to review proposed DPA addendum language (I'll share a draft in the next message).
- Procurement to flag any SLA exceptions (Ben will loop back with pricing impact if an SLA change is required).

We can target a candidate DPA addendum by EOD tomorrow; if that looks good we can push a DocuSign link and a short evidence-delivery schedule.

Best,
Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@mediflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 12:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks: no-train + KMS residency + subprocessor list

Alex / team —

Quick operational clarifications from the ops/security side so the artifacts line up with Mediflow's checklist:

- Evidence bundle we can produce within 3 business days after contract:
  * Subprocessor manifest (CSV) with roles + data access level.
  * Export of account-level capture flags showing "no-capture" / disabled training toggles for your account (timestamped).
  * Audit snapshot for a given 7-day window: request logs, model routing trace, and training-pipeline isolation manifest.
  * KMS proof: key metadata export and confirmation of customer-managed key association.

- Implementation notes / options:
  * Onshore KMS: recommended path is customer-managed KMS in AWS GovCloud / US East/West depending on your preference — we'll document precise region support, but we can support US-only key residency.
  * Data egress/export: we can provide SFTP export (encrypted) or a signed drive link for handoff; we recommend SFTP for procurement's ingestion pipelines.
  * Fallbacks: if you need additional assurance, we can offer a canary model variant that runs in an isolated tenant; this preserves latency SLAs and avoids cross-tenant spillover.

I'll attach a draft runbook (ops_runbook_draft.pdf) that maps each contractual obligation to the artifact we will deliver and who on Redwood owns that delivery. Ben — if Mediflow signs and wants accelerated delivery, we'll need a short implementation window and an engineering kick-off.

Kim
Senior Security Programs, Redwood Inference

Attachments: no-train-evidence-checklist.pdf; ops_runbook_draft.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@mediflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@mediflow.com>; Procurement <procurement@mediflow.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks: no-train + KMS residency + subprocessor list

Thanks — that is exactly the level of detail our security team wanted. A couple of small asks before we move to legal review and procurement:

- Can you include a one-paragraph description in the DPA addendum that explicitly states the operational controls that enforce "no-train" and points to the evidence artifacts (we need the doc to stand on its own for external reviewers).
- Procurement asks for a notional SLA exception summary if we require onshore KMS (we don't want open-ended SLA changes).
- Please include the HubSpot deal id and a proposed DocuSign link in your next email so Procurement can track and expedite.

If you can push the DPA addendum + DocuSign by tomorrow EOD we'll aim to sign mid-next-week and schedule the engineering kick-off for the week after.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Security & Privacy, Mediflow Health
alex.johnson@mediflow.com
